newsitem.title: HUNGARY: TVK HOPES HUF 5BLN FROM APV, SEES EXPANSION.
newsitem.headline: TVK HOPES HUF 5BLN FROM APV, SEES EXPANSION.

text.p: Hungarian chemicals company Tiszai Vegyi Kombinat Rt (TVK) said on Friday it was hoping to receive a sum of five billion forints under a provision of the privatisation law.

"We're negotiating with (privatisation agency) APV Rt about details of the five billion forints, the question is the precise amount and the schedule of payments," TVK's CEO Miklos Varhegyi told a news conference.
"There aren't any signs that APV would not pay this amount this year."
Varhegyi, speaking ahead of TVK's annual shareholders meeting to be held next Tuesday, said, however, the amount would help TVK to accelerate its development plans.

"We don't build our development plans on this amount," he said, adding that the use of the money could accelerate the procedure aimed at reducing TVK's exposure on the medium term to petrolchemical trends.
In TVK's sales petrochemical products account for 90 percent and plastics products for 10 percent. "We would like to improve this ratio substantially in favour of plastics."
Varhegyi said one of the company's key targets for 1997 was to meet rising demand on the local market.
"In 1997, in line with our strategy, we want to use opportunities stemming from the increasing domestic demand for our products," Varhegyi said.
The reason behind TVK's aim to boost business in Hungary was that domestic sales offer a higher gross profit, he said.

"At the same time we continue to improve the efficiency of our exports which are a declining proportion," he said, adding that the further development of TVK's network of foreign-registered companies was helping this aim.
Of its total sales, TVK generated 48 percent on the local market in 1995 and 53 percent in 1996, he said.

"The increasing domestic demand signals the increase of economic activity," Varhegyi said. "For us this (increasing domestic demand) justifies that the pace of plastics consumption exceeds the GDP growth."
In 1996 Hungary's GDP grew by around one percent, showing an increasing growth rate from quarter to quarter.

Varhegyi said TVK, which is to complete the recontruction of its olefin plant in the summer, and is going to start to prepare for investments aimed at a capacity increase of around 15 percent at the plant.
"Partly because of the reconstruction of the olefin plant we sacrificed our results in 1996," Varhegyi said, adding that the olefin plant did not operate for five weeks due to this.
In 1996 TVK posted an IAS unconsolidated net income of 7.69 billion forints, down from 10.47 billion in 1995.

Varhegyi declined to give a forecast for 1997, but said that the strong performance reached in the first quarter could be maintained through the year with prices in both raw materials and ready products seemed to remain stable.
"The market seems to be stable in both respects," he said. "There aren't any factors which would trigger any dramatic price changes in either (raw material prices and finished products.)
